title: URL Shortener
description: Design a service like bit.ly that takes long URLs and returns short, unique links that redirect to the original.
hints: Estimate: 100M URLs/month, 100:1 read-to-write ratio
Use base62 encoding for short codes
Cache popular redirects in Redis
checklist: Database schema and ID generation strategy

title: Pastebin
description: Design a text sharing service where users paste content and get a unique URL to share.
hints: Content can be large — consider object storage
Expiration policies for old pastes
Rate limit creation to prevent abuse
checklist: Max paste size and expiration policy

title: Rate Limiter
description: Design a distributed rate limiter that restricts API calls per user/IP to N requests per minute.
hints: Token bucket or sliding window algorithms
Redis for distributed counter state
Return 429 with Retry-After header

title: Notification Service
description: Design a service that sends push notifications, emails, and SMS to users based on events.
hints: Queue-based async processing for each channel
Template engine for message content
User preference management (opt-out)
checklist: Message queue per channel or unified?

title: Distributed Cache
description: Design a distributed in-memory cache like Redis Cluster with consistent hashing and replication.
hints: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes
Replication factor of 2-3 for availability
Cache eviction: LRU or LFU

title: Search Engine
description: Design a web search engine that crawls, indexes, and ranks pages for user queries.
hints: Inverted index for term → document mapping
MapReduce or streaming for index building
PageRank or similar for ranking

title: Distributed Job Scheduler
description: Design a system that schedules and executes millions of recurring and one-time jobs reliably.
hints: Time-wheel or priority queue for scheduling
Leader election for scheduler coordination
At-least-once execution with idempotency

title: Real-time Chat (WhatsApp/Slack)
description: Design a messaging platform supporting 1:1 and group chats with real-time delivery and offline sync.
hints: WebSockets for real-time, push notifications for offline
Message ordering within a conversation
Fan-out on write vs fan-out on read for groups

title: Video Streaming (YouTube/Netflix)
description: Design a video upload, transcoding, and streaming platform serving millions of concurrent viewers.
hints: CDN for video delivery, adaptive bitrate streaming
Transcoding pipeline with job queues
Separate metadata DB from blob storage
checklist: View count and analytics at scale

title: Ride Sharing (Uber)
description: Design a ride-sharing platform matching riders with nearby drivers in real time.
hints: Geospatial indexing (QuadTree, Geohash, S2)
WebSocket for driver location updates
Surge pricing based on supply/demand

title: Distributed Database
description: Design a distributed SQL database with automatic sharding, replication, and cross-shard queries.
hints: Shard by tenant or hash of primary key
Two-phase commit or Sagas for cross-shard transactions
Raft for shard leader election

title: Distributed Filesystem
description: Design a distributed filesystem like Google File System or HDFS for storing petabytes across commodity hardware.
hints: Metadata server separate from data nodes
Chunk replication (default 3x)
Append-only writes for efficiency

title: LLM Inference Platform
description: Design a multi-tenant LLM inference platform with continuous batching, autoscaling GPUs, and cost-per-token metering.
hints: Separate prefill and decode if traffic mix warrants it
Track KV cache memory as a first-class resource
Meter tokens, not only requests
rubric: Correctly models KV cache / memory pressure
Defines SLOs for latency and availability

title: Enterprise RAG Search
description: Design a RAG system over millions of private documents with hybrid retrieval, ACL-aware ranking, and evals.
hints: Chunking and metadata matter as much as the embedding model
Enforce ACLs at retrieval time
Evals as CI for regressions

title: Coding Agent Platform
description: Design a coding agent platform with sandboxed tool execution, durable workflows, and permissioning.
hints: Treat tool calls as idempotent where possible
Sandbox untrusted code execution
Persist agent state for long runs

title: Exchange Matching Engine
description: Design a low-latency matching engine with fair ordering, deterministic replay, and risk checks.
hints: Determinism enables replay and audit
Separate market data fanout from matching
Pre-trade risk must not become a hidden latency cliff

title: Notification System (Advanced)
description: Design a scalable, multi-channel notification system handling push, email, SMS, and in-app alerts for 500M+ users with per-user preferences, deduplication, and guaranteed delivery.
hints: Fan-out fan-in: publish one event, fan-out per channel, aggregate delivery receipts
Use priority queues to separate critical (OTP, security) from bulk (marketing) notifications
Store a notification inbox in Cassandra keyed by user_id for in-app retrieval
Deduplication window: check a Redis bloom filter before enqueuing to avoid duplicate sends
Respect per-user quiet hours by scheduling delivery into a future-time bucket
checklist: Define channel types: push (APNs/FCM), email (SES/SendGrid), SMS (Twilio), in-app
Capacity estimate: 500M users, 10 notifications/user/day, peak burst factor
Event ingestion: single event bus (Kafka) fans out to per-channel workers
User preference service: opt-outs, frequency caps, quiet hours, language/locale
Delivery guarantee: at-least-once with idempotency tokens, dead-letter queue
Deduplication: bloom filter or Redis set keyed on (event_id, user_id, channel)
Status tracking: sent → delivered → opened pipeline, analytics aggregation
Rate limiting per third-party provider (APNs, Twilio) to avoid bans
rubric: Fan-out strategy (write-time vs read-time) is explicitly justified
Deduplication mechanism prevents double-delivery across retries
Provider rate limits and backpressure are handled
Failure modes: provider down, user device unreachable, queue overflow
scaleVariants: Support 100k notifications/second during a flash sale event
Add multi-region: route users to nearest notification cluster
Introduce templating engine with A/B variant selection

title: News Feed (Twitter/Instagram)
description: Design a personalized news feed that aggregates posts from followed accounts and surfaces them in reverse-chronological or ranked order with low latency.
hints: Fan-out on write (push) works for most users; fan-out on read (pull) for celebrity accounts
Pre-compute feeds using an async worker so reads are O(1) from a user feed cache
Score posts with a ranking model that considers recency, engagement, and relationship strength
Use Redis sorted sets (ZSET) keyed by user_id to store feed post IDs with score = timestamp
Celebrity problem: >1M followers → skip write fan-out; merge at read time from celebrity timeline
checklist: Functional scope: who can post, follow, what content types (text, images, videos)
Capacity estimate: 300M DAU, 5 posts/user/day, 500 followers avg, celebrity tail
Fan-out model chosen and justified (push vs pull vs hybrid)
Feed storage: Redis ZSET per user, capped at 1000 entries with TTL
Ranking: chronological baseline, optional ML scorer microservice
Pagination: cursor-based keyset pagination, not offset
Consistency trade-off: eventual consistency acceptable for feed updates
Cache warming for new users and re-login after cache eviction
rubric: Fan-out model justified with capacity numbers
Read latency target met with proposed cache architecture
Stale feed scenario and refresh strategy described
scaleVariants: Add algorithmic ranking replacing pure chronological order
Support 10% of users with >100k followers (celebrity tier)
Extend to multi-media feed (video thumbnails, story rings)

title: Distributed Lock Service
description: Design a distributed lock service that provides mutual exclusion across processes and machines, with TTL-based expiry, fencing tokens, and high availability.
hints: Use Redlock (5-node Redis quorum) for AP lock or Zookeeper/etcd for CP semantics
Always return a fencing token (monotonically increasing version) with each lock grant
Lock TTL must be much shorter than the critical section duration to avoid false expiry
Processes must re-validate fencing token before committing the guarded resource
Distinguish lock acquire timeout from lock hold timeout in your API
checklist: Define semantics: advisory vs mandatory, reentrant or not
Choose consistency model: CP (etcd/ZooKeeper) vs AP (Redlock) with trade-off rationale
Fencing token mechanism to handle zombie processes holding stale locks
TTL and heartbeat renewal to auto-release locks from crashed holders
Lock wait queue: fair FIFO or try-and-fail with exponential backoff
Observability: lock contention metrics, holder identity, wait time histograms
rubric: CP vs AP choice is justified with concrete failure scenario
Fencing tokens prevent split-brain writes on the guarded resource
TTL and renewal heartbeat prevent indefinite lock holds
Clock skew and network partition failure modes are addressed
scaleVariants: Scale to 1M lock operations/second across thousands of distinct resources
Add lock hierarchy to avoid deadlocks across nested critical sections
Support read-write locks (shared/exclusive) in addition to exclusive locks

title: Metrics & Time-Series Database
description: Design a time-series metrics store (like Prometheus + Thanos or InfluxDB) that ingests billions of data points per day, supports range queries, and retains data with configurable downsampling.
hints: Store metrics as (metric_name, label_set, timestamp, value); label_set is the high-cardinality enemy
Chunk time series into fixed-window blocks (e.g., 2h) for compact columnar storage
Use delta-of-delta + XOR compression (Gorilla encoding) for timestamps and float values
Inverted index on label key=value pairs for fast series lookup during query
Downsampling: keep 1-min resolution for 15 days, 5-min for 90 days, 1-hour forever
checklist: Ingestion path: write-ahead log → in-memory head block → periodic flush to disk blocks
Series cardinality management: reject or cap very high-cardinality label sets
Compression scheme (Gorilla or similar) for time and value columns
Query engine: PromQL-style range queries, aggregation, rate() computation
Long-term storage: compact blocks uploaded to object storage (S3)
Query federation across multiple TSDB instances for global view
Alerting integration: rules evaluated against recent data with sub-minute latency
rubric: Compression strategy meaningfully reduces storage vs naive approach
Query path latency target met with proposed index structure
Retention and downsampling pipeline is operationally coherent
scaleVariants: 10x ingestion rate: 10B data points per day across 10M active series
Global federation: query across 20 regional TSDB clusters in a single request
Add anomaly detection pipeline on top of the ingestion stream

title: Collaborative Document Editor
description: Design a real-time collaborative document editor like Google Docs that lets multiple users edit the same document simultaneously with conflict-free merges and persistent history.
hints: Operational Transformation (OT) or CRDTs (e.g., YATA, RGA) are the two main approaches to conflict resolution
CRDTs simplify peer-to-peer architectures but have higher memory overhead; OT requires a central server for ordering
Store document as an event log (operations), not full snapshots, for efficient history and undo
Cursor and selection presence should be broadcast via a separate lightweight presence channel
Checkpoint snapshots periodically to avoid replaying the full operation log on load
checklist: Choose concurrency model: OT with server authority vs CRDT with peer broadcast
Operation model: insert(pos, char), delete(pos, len), retain(len) or character-level CRDT nodes
Real-time transport: WebSocket per document session, reconnect with catch-up replay
Persistent storage: operation log in Postgres/Cassandra, snapshots in object storage
Presence service: who is online, cursor positions, named selections (ephemeral, Redis pub/sub)
Undo/redo: per-user undo stack that composes with concurrent operations correctly
Access control: owner, editor, commenter, viewer roles enforced at operation application
Export pipeline: render document state to DOCX, PDF on demand
rubric: Concurrency model (OT vs CRDT) chosen and trade-offs articulated
Convergence guarantee: all clients reach identical document state after network partition
Latency: local edits reflected instantly (optimistic), remote edits merged within 200ms
Data model supports full edit history, comments, and undo without redesign
scaleVariants: Scale to 1000 simultaneous editors on a single large document
Add offline editing with sync-on-reconnect using CRDT merge
Support structured content: spreadsheet cells, drawing canvas alongside text

title: Video Streaming CDN
description: Design the CDN layer for a video streaming platform — including edge cache hierarchy, adaptive bitrate selection, segment pre-fetching, and cache eviction — to serve petabytes of video globally with sub-second start time.
hints: Split manifest (.m3u8/.mpd) delivery from segment delivery: manifests are tiny and can be served with stricter caching rules
Use consistent hashing at edge PoPs to route a given video's segments to a predictable set of cache servers
Pre-warm edge caches for anticipated high-demand content (live events, viral uploads) using a push CDN model
Byte-range requests allow partial segment caching; store segments as immutable objects keyed by (video_id, resolution, segment_index)
ABR algorithm (e.g., BOLA, MPC) runs in the client player and selects bitrate based on measured bandwidth and buffer level
checklist: CDN topology: origin → regional PoP → edge PoP → client, with cache-fill hierarchy
Segment naming convention and immutability guarantee for effective caching
Cache eviction policy per edge node: LRU with popularity boosting (LFU hybrid)
Live vs VOD distinction: live requires low-latency segment availability at edge
Failover: edge miss → parent PoP → origin, with timeout budgets at each hop
Bandwidth estimation and adaptive bitrate ladder (e.g., 240p, 480p, 720p, 1080p, 4K)
DRM and signed URL token validation at edge without origin round-trip
Analytics: rebuffering ratio, start time, bitrate switches reported per session
rubric: Cache hit ratio strategy is quantified with expected storage vs bandwidth saved
Live streaming latency path is distinct from VOD and meets <10s end-to-end delay
Failure modes (edge node down, origin overload) have clear fallback paths
Security: DRM and token auth prevent unauthorized segment download
scaleVariants: Support a simultaneous live event with 50M concurrent viewers
Add multi-CDN failover: automatically route around a provider outage
Optimize for mobile-first markets with high packet loss and low bandwidth

title: Multiplayer Game Session Service
description: Design a backend service that manages real-time multiplayer game sessions: matchmaking, game server allocation, authoritative state sync, and session lifecycle for a 10M DAU action game.
hints: Authoritative server model prevents cheating; clients send inputs, server sends canonical state
Client-side prediction + rollback reconciliation hides network latency from the player
Match state is ephemeral — store it in memory on the game server, only persist final results to DB
Game servers are stateful; use a session directory (Redis) to map session_id → game server address
UDP with custom reliability (e.g., QUIC or ENet) beats TCP for low-latency state updates
checklist: Matchmaking service: skill-based (ELO/Glicko), queue timeout, party grouping
Game server fleet management: allocate from warm pool, scale on queue depth
Session registry: Redis mapping session_id → game server IP:port with TTL
Network protocol: UDP/QUIC for game state, WebSocket for lobby/chat
Client-side prediction and server reconciliation (rollback netcode or state interpolation)
Session lifecycle: lobby → in-game → post-game summary → cleanup
Cheat detection: server-authoritative validation of all inputs
Persistent storage: match results, replay file, stats delta written post-game
rubric: Authoritative server model is justified and cheat surface minimized
Latency mitigation (prediction + rollback) is clearly described
Game server fleet scales to absorb burst demand within seconds
Session failure (server crash mid-game) has a defined recovery or compensation path
scaleVariants: Scale to 1M concurrent sessions during a major tournament event
Support cross-region lobbies where players span 3+ continents
Add spectator mode: broadcast authoritative state to 10k viewers per match

title: Feature Flag Service
description: Design a feature flag (feature toggle) service that enables trunk-based development, percentage rollouts, A/B experiments, and kill switches with sub-millisecond evaluation latency.
hints: Evaluate flags client-side from a local in-process cache; never call the flag service on the hot path
Push flag config updates via SSE or WebSocket so SDK caches refresh within seconds of a change
Target rules: user_id, cohort, region, plan tier — store as a decision tree serialized to JSON
Assignment must be sticky: same user always gets the same variant — hash(user_id + flag_key) % 100
Audit log every flag change with who, what, when — critical for debugging production incidents
checklist: Flag model: boolean toggle, multivariate (A/B/C), and gradual percentage rollout
Targeting rules: user attributes, segments, anonymous users (device ID)
SDK architecture: local in-process evaluation against a cached config snapshot
Config delivery: polling (simple) vs streaming SSE (low-latency updates)
Stickiness: deterministic assignment via hashing ensures consistent user experience
Kill switch: immediate global disable with <1s propagation SLA
Experiment analysis: impression and conversion event collection for statistical significance
Audit log and change history with rollback capability
rubric: Flag evaluation is local (sub-millisecond) with no synchronous network call
Stickiness mechanism guarantees consistent variant per user across SDKs
Config propagation latency is bounded and meets the stated SLA
Experiment integrity: assignment cannot be gamed by user-supplied attributes
scaleVariants: Scale to 500M flag evaluations per second across all SDK instances
Add multi-environment support: dev, staging, prod with promotion workflow
Integrate with a stats engine for real-time experiment significance alerts

title: Secret Manager
description: Design a secret management service like HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager that stores, rotates, and audits credentials with fine-grained access control and zero long-lived plaintext exposure.
hints: Envelope encryption: each secret encrypted with a data encryption key (DEK), DEK encrypted with a key encryption key (KEK) stored in an HSM or KMS
Seal/unseal ceremony: master key sharded via Shamir Secret Sharing so no single operator can unseal alone
Dynamic secrets: generate short-lived DB credentials on demand rather than storing static passwords
Every read and write must produce an immutable audit log entry — this is non-negotiable for compliance
Lease and renewal model: clients get a lease token; server revokes on expiry or explicit revoke call
checklist: Encryption model: envelope encryption with DEK/KEK hierarchy and HSM/KMS backing
Authentication backends: IAM role, Kubernetes service account, LDAP, AppRole
Authorization model: policy as code (HCL/YAML) with path-based ACLs
Dynamic secrets engine: on-demand credential generation for databases, cloud IAM
Secret versioning and rollback for safe rotation
Lease lifecycle: TTL, renewal, revocation, and cascading revocation on compromise
Audit log: append-only, tamper-evident (WORM storage or Merkle chain)
High availability: Raft consensus cluster, sealed state on startup
rubric: Encryption at rest and in transit leaves no plaintext secret on disk
Access control model is least-privilege and testable by policy unit tests
Rotation and revocation paths work without downtime for consuming services
Compromise scenario: leaked DEK does not expose all secrets (KEK isolation)
scaleVariants: Scale to 100k secret read requests per second across 10k services
Add cross-region replication with strong consistency for secret writes
Support BYOK (bring your own key) for enterprise tenants with their own HSMs

title: Webhook Delivery Service
description: Design a reliable webhook delivery system that sends HTTP callbacks to customer-registered endpoints with guaranteed at-least-once delivery, retry backoff, signature verification, and observability.
hints: Decouple event production from delivery: publish events to Kafka, workers consume and attempt delivery
Exponential backoff with jitter: retry at 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s … up to 24h before moving to DLQ
Sign each payload with HMAC-SHA256 using the endpoint's secret; customer verifies the X-Signature header
Track delivery status per (event_id, endpoint_id): pending → delivered / failed / dlq
Circuit breaker per endpoint: after N consecutive failures, pause delivery and alert the customer
checklist: Event ingestion: producers publish to Kafka; consumer workers handle delivery
Endpoint registry: customer-registered URLs, secrets, event type subscriptions
Retry policy: exponential backoff, max attempts, dead-letter queue after exhaustion
Idempotency: include event_id in payload; customer endpoint should deduplicate
Payload signing: HMAC-SHA256, include timestamp to prevent replay attacks
Circuit breaker per endpoint to avoid hammering consistently failing URLs
Delivery log: immutable record of all attempts (timestamp, status code, response body snippet)
Dashboard and alerting: failed delivery rate per endpoint, DLQ depth
rubric: At-least-once delivery is guaranteed even across worker restarts
Retry storm is prevented by backoff + jitter and circuit breaker
Security: signature scheme prevents payload tampering and replay
Customer visibility: delivery log is accessible via API and UI
scaleVariants: Scale to 1M webhook deliveries per minute across 100k customer endpoints
Add fan-out: a single internal event triggers webhooks to multiple subscribers
Support ordered delivery per endpoint with a per-endpoint serial queue

title: LLM Chat Service with Tool Calling
description: Design a production LLM chat service that supports multi-turn conversations, tool/function calling, streaming responses, and durable session history for millions of users.
hints: Streaming: use server-sent events (SSE) to push tokens to the client as they are generated; never buffer a full response
Tool execution is synchronous within the model loop: model emits tool_call → service executes tool → result injected into context → model continues
Context window management: when history exceeds token budget, summarize older turns or use sliding window with lossless compression of system instructions
Persist conversation turns in a append-only store (DynamoDB or Cassandra) keyed by (session_id, turn_index)
Rate limit at the token level, not just request level, to control GPU cost per user
checklist: Session model: session_id, system prompt, turn history, tool registry per session
Streaming transport: SSE for browser, gRPC stream for server-to-server
Tool registry: manifest of available tools (name, description, JSON schema), dispatched to sandboxed executors
Context window management: token counting, summarization or eviction strategy
Tool execution safety: sandboxed, timeout-bounded, with output size limits
Conversation persistence: append-only turn store for history retrieval and audit
Token metering: prompt tokens + completion tokens logged per user per request
Fallback and error handling: model timeout, tool failure, context overflow
rubric: Streaming latency to first token is minimized and not blocked by tool calls
Tool execution is safe: cannot access resources outside declared permissions
Context management strategy does not silently drop critical conversation context
Cost and latency SLOs are stated and the design shows how they are met
scaleVariants: Support 100k concurrent streaming sessions with sub-500ms time-to-first-token
Add multi-modal tool calls: image input, file upload, code execution sandbox
Implement long-term memory: persist and retrieve relevant past conversations via vector search

title: Autocomplete / Typeahead Service
description: Design a low-latency autocomplete service that returns ranked suggestions within 50ms as users type in a search box, supporting billions of queries per day and personalised results.
hints: Trie or prefix hash index (Radix tree) for sub-millisecond prefix lookup; persist to disk with serialization
Top-K suggestions per prefix: store (prefix → sorted list of top-K completions by score) in Redis for direct O(1) lookup
Aggregate query logs daily to update suggestion scores via a MapReduce/Spark job feeding back into the index
Personalization layer: re-rank top-K using user history, location, and language after prefix lookup
Cache warmup: pre-compute and cache suggestions for the most popular 10M prefixes at deploy time
checklist: Index structure: Trie vs prefix table in Redis; trade-offs in memory and update latency
Scoring: global popularity + recency + user personalization signal weights
Query path: edge PoP cache → Redis prefix table → (miss) Trie service → response
Index update pipeline: event log → Spark aggregation → incremental prefix table update
Latency budget: <50ms p99 at 100k QPS including network round-trip
Filtering: exclude adult/illegal content, apply SafeSearch at suggestion generation time
Multi-language and locale support: separate indexes or locale-aware prefix normalization
Fallback: return most popular global suggestions when personalization service is degraded
rubric: Latency target (<50ms) is met by the described index + caching architecture
Index update frequency balances freshness with write amplification cost
Personalization is applied without blocking the critical read path
Safety filtering is applied before suggestions reach the client
scaleVariants: Scale to 1M QPS globally with <20ms p99 using edge caching
Add real-time trending: surface queries spiking in the last 60 seconds
Support entity-aware autocomplete: distinguish queries from named entities (people, products)

title: Payment Ledger
description: Design a double-entry payment ledger system that records all financial transactions with immutability, strong consistency, idempotency, and auditability, processing millions of transactions per day.
hints: Double-entry bookkeeping: every transaction debits one account and credits another; sum of all entries must always be zero
Idempotency key on every write: clients include a UUID; server deduplicates using a unique index on idempotency_key
Use a serializable isolation level (or optimistic locking) to prevent double-spend and race conditions
Immutability: ledger entries are never updated or deleted; reversals are new credit/debit entries with a reference to the original
Partition ledger by account_id for horizontal scale; cross-partition transfers require two-phase commit or Saga
checklist: Data model: accounts table, ledger_entries table (account_id, amount, currency, type, idempotency_key, created_at)
Double-entry invariant enforcement: application-level and database constraint checks
Idempotency: unique constraint on idempotency_key with upsert-or-return-existing semantics
Concurrency control: optimistic locking on account balance or serializable transactions
Multi-currency support: store amounts in minor units (cents), handle FX conversion rates
Saga pattern for distributed transfers: debit source → (failure rollback) → credit destination
Reconciliation job: nightly balance check, cross-system reconciliation with payment processors
Audit log: immutable append-only trail queryable by account, time range, and transaction type
rubric: Double-entry invariant is enforced at the database level, not just application level
Idempotency prevents double charges even under network retries
Concurrency model prevents overdraft and race conditions under load
Failure scenario: partial transfer failure leaves system in consistent, recoverable state
scaleVariants: Scale to 100k transactions per second while maintaining ACID guarantees
Add multi-currency real-time FX conversion with rate lock window
Support multi-tenant ledger: isolate balances per merchant while sharing infrastructure
